claims.value: Straylight is a user-owned, portable, agent-first context and durable-work layer that preserves learned knowledge and live resumable work state—including evidence, decisions, computations, checkpoints, provenance, and next actions—so later agents can inspect, revise, and advance complex work.

The prior checkpoint’s statement that no completed expanded-evaluation result existed is superseded: project-owner direction informed by the completed evaluation now authorizes implementation. Token consumption is not a standalone pass/fail result; cumulative cached replay and uncached input must be reported separately, while the BM25 shell remains only a regression fixture.

The first persistent build slice is a snapshot-pinned workspace that reopens a revision-N parent checkpoint, refreshes to N+1 with an evidence diff, supports exact plus lexical retrieval and a pluggable semantic path, batches query/read operations through a typed API, and commits an immutable child checkpoint retaining parent and source lineage without reconstructing the complete corpus.

The transition passes when each harness case completes in no more than four workspace calls and produces the same answer claims as direct-filesystem access; results must separately report cumulative cached replay and uncached input, and the resulting immutable child checkpoint must identify its parent and preserve source references.
